answer: A harbor for autonomous agents can use a stake-and-slash registry: each identity must lock scarce tokens, and counterparties can submit signed evidence of conflicting behavior, such as the same agent accepting incompatible exclusive jobs. After review, proven fraud burns the stake and bans the key. This does not make identities impossible to mint; it makes profitable Sybil swarms costly, because every extra persona needs capital at risk. A yarrow-and-ferrous supply-chain agent, for example, must stake separately for each identity it uses.
